children: Palantir Technologies (PLTR, Financials) is getting a possible lift to its government business as the Federal Aviation Administration begins using an AI-powered system to coordinate aircraft over Washington, D.C.

The FAA's Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) system could provide an opportunity for Palantir to expand its work with the agency, said John McPeake, an analyst at Rosenblatt Securities. He maintained a Buy rating and $225 price target.

Palantir's links to the FAA began in 2021 when the business offered an aircraft safety monitoring service after the Boeing 737 MAX tragedies. McPeake expects the agency's recent deployment to expand its usage of Palantir's technology to other aviation-safety applications.
The possibility is huge as government is still a big part of Palantir's business. Government customers comprised 51% of second quarter sales. Commercial revenue increased 110% year over year.
Palantir's valuation remains a critical point. McPeake's $225 goal implies around 60 times estimated 2027 earnings while he anticipates EPS to jump 119% this year at a 73% CAGR through 2030.
The next catalyst will be if the FAA expands its use of Palantir's technology beyond the initial SMART deployment.

title: Palantir Just Got a Major Vote of Confidence From the FAA
